1.explanation: This script uses the official Lighthouse Node API together with chrome-launcher. It launches a headless Chrome instance, runs only the “best-practices” category (which contains the Minify JavaScript audit), and prints out the displayValue for the minification audit plus the entire stackPacks array. When executed against https://abcnews.go.com/ with the currently shipped js-library-detector Fast-Path integration, you will see two identical React entries in the stackPacks output, reproducing the duplicated stack-pack bug.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse (or PageSpeed Insights) against https://abcnews.go.com/ and inspecting the “Minify JavaScript” audit under the “Best Practices” category, you’ll see two identical React stack-pack entries (same icon, title, and help text) rendered one after the other. In the JSON output there are two items in lhr.stackPacks both with id “react” – one from the regular detector and one from the new “Fast Path” experimental checks.
